subject: Customer encryption model + next technical validation steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@medcura.com>
Cc: Anil Desai <anil.desai@medcura.com>, MedCura Security <security@medcura.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: encryption surface + BYOK options (post-demo)

Hi Priyanka / Anil —

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear breakdown on MedCura’s regulatory scope (HIPAA primary, data residency in us-east-1, selective EU PII), and the three core asks you outlined:

- SOC 2 attestation timing and scope (app + infra)
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) for PHI at rest and in backups
- Clarification on in-transit protections across internal integrations and S3 replication

Recap & asks from our side to validate the model and scope next week:

1) SOC 2: can you confirm whether you need Redwood to provide our Type II report by Q3, or if a SOC 2 bridge letter will suffice for procurement? A short answer will help prioritize legal.

2) BYOK: high-level choices we support — 1) Redwood-managed CMKs (default), 2) Customer-supplied KMS keys (BYOK via customer KMS with cross-account CMK permissions), 3) HSM-backed customer keys (external HSM/HSM-as-a-service where customer holds root). For MedCura, please indicate preferred model (option 1/2/3) and whether key rotation policies (30/90/365 days) are mandated.

3) Key scoping: do you need per-tenant keys (one key per customer space) or a single key per environment (prod/staging)? If per-tenant, how many active tenants do you expect initially?

4) Backups & exports: are you requiring encrypted backups with customer key wrap? If yes, share any retention/GDPR deletion requirements that would affect key lifecycle.

5) Integration touchpoints: we’ll need a short network diagram showing where PHI touches third-party systems (you attached one today) — can you drop the current diagram into the Drive link above?

I attached a short vendor questionnaire (PDF) with specific KMS/HSM questions; if your security team prefers, we can jump on a 30-min tech validation call with our crypto lead (Marissa) and Rishi to nail the details.

Proposed next steps:
- You: indicate BYOK preference + key scoping answers (items 2–4) — by Thu 24th if possible.
- We: schedule a 30-min technical validation with Marissa/Rishi the week of Jun 28th; I’ll send possible times after I hear your preference.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.k@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@medcura.com>

Cc: Anil Desai <anil.desai@medcura.com>, MedCura Security <security@medcura.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: encryption surface + BYOK options (post-demo)

Hi Vivek — thanks for the detailed recap and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline below and attaching the network diagram we referenced.

1) SOC 2: We will require Redwood’s Type II report for our legal/compliance review; a bridge letter won’t be sufficient for now. Target date for us is to receive it before contracting (end of Q3).

2) BYOK: Preference is option 2 (customer-supplied KMS keys with cross-account IAM). We run AWS KMS in our account and would like to maintain key material under our control. Rotation policy: 365 days is preferred but 90 days is acceptable if required for compatibility.

3) Key scoping: We need per-tenant keys for PHI isolation. Initially ~12 tenants, scale to 50 in year 1.

4) Backups: Yes — backups must be encrypted and wrapped with the customer key. Retention is 7 years for PHI backups; deletion requests must be honored per our data retention policy (we’ll provide the DLP clause).

5) Integration touchpoints: attaching current internal diagram (network-segmentation.png). Security has also flagged one requirement: any KMS cross-account role must be limited to encryption/decryption for the specific Redwood service principal and logged to our CloudTrail with aggregation to our Splunk instance.

We’re happy to do a technical validation call. Can you propose times for Jun 29–30? Our security lead (Anil) will be on the call.

Thanks — Priyanka

Attachments: MedCura_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf, network-segmentation.png

--
Priyanka Shah
VP Product & Security Programs, MedCura Health
priyanka@medcura.com | +1 (617) 555-0221
From: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: encryption surface + BYOK options (pricing implications)

Looping Rishi — Priyanka confirmed BYOK via customer KMS and per-tenant keys (~12 initial). Rishi, can you weight the ops and cost delta for per-tenant BYOK (AWS KMS cross-account) vs Redwood-managed CMKs with envelope encryption? High level answers we need for procurement:

- Incremental monthly cost estimate (kms request/crypto ops + any HSM rental if needed)
- Impact on backup/export workflows (extra steps, latency)
- Any SLA gotchas (key rotation windows, cross-account role availability)

Vivek — if you can draft two short options (Redwood-managed + BYOK-per-tenant) we’ll send procurement both. I suggest we also push our SOC 2 Type II report link to MedCura legal once it’s available.

Thanks, Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions & GTM, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: encryption surface + BYOK options (pricing implications)

Thanks — quick notes from infra/ops perspective:

- BYOK per-tenant (AWS KMS cross-account): increases KMS API usage proportional to active tenants and request rate. For MedCura’s expected scale (12 tenants, low single-digit qps), monthly KMS cost is modest (~$300–600) but includes CloudTrail ingestion and cross-account role setup.
- Envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys: lower customer ops, predictable unit cost but less control for customer. If MedCura insists on full key custody we should offer HSM-backed BYOK as premium (adds managed HSM fees and complexity).
- Backups: wrapping backups with customer key adds an extra encryption/decryption step in export/restore flows; negligible latency for bulk operations but requires key availability windows for scheduled restores. We must document key rotation process (automated rotation vs manual) and ensure we surface key errors in our console for their security team.
- SLA: cross-account KMS role availability is usually fine; the main SLA risk is if customer disables the key or revokes IAM access — we should add a clause about operational responsibilities and notification windows.

Action items: Vivek — draft two options with short bullets and attach a redlined contract clause for key responsibilities. Marissa should be on the technical validation call to confirm HSM compatibility if MedCura requests it.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
